key_insight: The paper reframes quantum generative modeling around how much magic an IQP circuit consumes, showing that output-distribution progress can be a better resource metric than state-space fidelity or geodesic distance.
engineering_relevance: This suggests IQP-based generators may offer a resource-efficient route to quantum advantage on early fault-tolerant hardware, especially if two-qubit gate overhead is kept under control.
method: Measures progress directly on the probability simplex rather than in projective Hilbert space.
Uses changes in Jensen-Shannon divergence to quantify magic consumption during training.
Evaluates trained random γ-sparse IQP circuits and compares them with phase-randomized states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports signatures of efficient magic use, with the dominant contribution coming from two-qubit gates and unusually low intermediate magic for IQP circuits at the same sampling distributions.
watch_item: The framework depends on distribution-level training behavior, so practical advantage may still be limited by circuit depth, two-qubit gate costs, and hardware noise.
paper_title: Generative AI Beyond Tokens: Quantum Resource Consumption of IQP Circuits
